findings.documented: Token expires in 86400 seconds (24 hours). There is no refresh flow. Response returns user with name and email.
findings.actual: Token expires in 900 seconds (15 minutes). Server returns refresh_token with refresh_url: /auth/refresh. User object contains only email, omitting name.
findings.how_found: Called POST /auth/login during authentication flow investigation and inspected JSON response fields.
findings.impact: User sessions expire silently after 15 minutes unless the undocumented refresh endpoint is handled. User display name cannot be sourced from login response.

findings.documented: Every request must carry the API key appended as a query parameter: ?api_key=IVY26-XXXXXXXXXXXX
findings.actual: Passing api_key as a query parameter returns 401 Unauthorized with message 'send your key in the X-API-Key request header, not as a query parameter'.
findings.how_found: Invoked /health and /auth/login with query parameter and captured 401 error response detail.
findings.impact: Any client implementing the documented query parameter authentication fails completely on every request.

findings.documented: POST /auth/logout invalidates the current token server side.
findings.actual: Server returns { ok: true, note: 'tokens are stateless; discard them client side' } without server-side session invalidation.
findings.how_found: Called POST /auth/logout with active bearer token and inspected response body and repeated subsequent calls with the same token.
findings.impact: Logout must be enforced on the client side by clearing persisted storage; tokens remain cryptographically valid until JWT expiration.

findings.documented: Every collection endpoint takes page (default 1) and limit (default 20, max 200). Response has total, page, page_size, results.
findings.actual: Server completely ignores 'page' parameter and requires 'offset'. Default and maximum limit is 50 (limits > 50 are capped at 50). Response format returns limit, offset, count, total, has_more, results.
findings.how_found: Called /v1/listings with page=2 and limit=200; observed offset remained 0, limit was capped at 50, and response metadata omitted page/page_size.
findings.impact: Clients requesting page-based pagination receive offset 0 repeatedly (endless loop of the first 50 records). Limits above 50 fail silently.

findings.documented: GET /v1/listings returns only active sale listings in your city. Inactive, expired and withdrawn listings are excluded server side.
findings.actual: Endpoint returns all 4,700 listings in the database, of which 978 records have is_live: false.
findings.how_found: Retrieved complete dataset and inspected is_live boolean distribution across all records.
findings.impact: Client must explicitly filter by is_live or display inactive property status badges to prevent users from viewing withdrawn listings.

findings.documented: total is the exact number of records matching your filters. To fetch every record, read total, divide by limit, and request that many pages.
findings.actual: Response metadata reports total: 4381, but paging beyond offset 4350 continues returning valid records until reaching offset 4700 (exactly 4,700 total retrievable records).
findings.how_found: Observed has_more: true at offset 4350 and continued pagination until offset 4650 yielded last records and offset 4700 returned count 0.
findings.impact: Clients relying on total metadata terminate pagination early and drop 319 active and valid listing records.

findings.actual: GET /v1/listing/{listing_id} returns 404 Not Found. The working endpoint is plural: GET /v1/listings/{listing_id}.
findings.how_found: Attempted fetching individual listings via singular path and reproduced 404; succeeded using plural path.
findings.impact: Direct listing detail page loads break with 404 errors if using the documented singular route.

findings.documented: GET /v1/listings/{listing_id}/similar returns up to ten comparable listings.
findings.how_found: Sent authenticated GET requests to both route variants across multiple valid listing IDs.
findings.impact: Similar properties section cannot rely on upstream API; backend must calculate comparable listings dynamically.

findings.documented: GET /v1/analytics/summary returns pre-computed aggregates for your city (total listings, median price, median price per sqft, breakdowns).
findings.actual: GET /v1/analytics/summary returns 404 Not Found. No /analytics or /summary endpoints exist.
findings.impact: Insights screen must compute genuine aggregations directly from empirical property datasets on the server.

findings.documented: GET /v1/favourites, POST /v1/favourites with body { id }, and DELETE /v1/favourites/{id} manage user saved properties.
findings.actual: All /v1/favourites and /favourites routes return 404 Not Found.
findings.how_found: Probed GET, POST, and DELETE requests with demo user authentication; received 404 Not Found.
findings.impact: Application-level favorites must be persisted in MongoDB associated with the authenticated user.

findings.documented: GET /v1/listings accepts min_price, max_price, and bedroom query parameters to filter listings.
findings.actual: min_price and max_price query parameters are quietly ignored by the server (total and results remain unchanged). The bedroom parameter is also ignored (bhk must be used instead).
findings.how_found: Queried /v1/listings?min_price=10000000&max_price=15000000 and received identical results and total (4,381) including properties outside the price window.
findings.impact: Listings search interface shows incorrect records unless client/server fallback filtering is applied.

findings.documented: GET /v1/listings accepts order parameter ('asc' or 'desc') for sort_by.
findings.actual: Passing order=desc is quietly ignored; server always returns ascending sort order regardless of the order argument.
findings.how_found: Queried /v1/listings?sort_by=price&order=desc and compared with order=asc; both returned identical items.
findings.impact: Users sorting by highest price or newest listings receive default ascending records unless client/backend sorts locally.

findings.documented: price_min and price_max are in rupees, integer, everywhere in the API.
findings.actual: In /v1/projects, price_min and price_max are stored as Lakhs (when >= 10) and Crores (when < 10) as floats/integers, not integer Rupees.
findings.how_found: Analyzed all 520 project records. Unconverted price_min exceeded price_max in 372 projects; converting values >= 10 as Lakhs and < 10 as Crores resolved 100% of price discrepancies.
findings.impact: Projects displayed directly with integer rupee formatting would show multi-crore luxury projects as costing ₹2 to ₹99.

findings.documented: Area: Square feet, integer, everywhere in the API.
findings.actual: 24 listings from MagicHomes (MAG-*) report carpet_area and super_built_up_area in square meters (values 35-49 sqm) rather than square feet.
findings.how_found: Filtered listings with carpet_area < 50; discovered 24 1-BHK/builder floors priced at 35-70 Lakhs with carpet areas between 35 and 49 sqm (376 to 527 sqft).
findings.impact: Displays absurdly small areas (e.g. 40 sqft apartment) and distorts price-per-square-foot calculations by a factor of 10.76 if unnormalized.

findings.documented: Every listing_id is globally unique, and each listing corresponds to exactly one physical property.
findings.actual: 11 distinct physical properties are duplicated across multiple syndication portals (e.g. dwelling, magichomes, 100acres) with different listing IDs and slightly different pricing.
findings.how_found: Grouped listings by (apartment_name, locality, bedroom, floor, carpet_area, facing_direction) and found 11 multi-record pairs.
findings.impact: Inventory counts overstate the true volume of physical real estate available by 11 units.

findings.documented: total_listings in /v1/projects is the number of listings currently available in the project, recomputed whenever a listing is added or withdrawn, always agreeing with /v1/listings?project_id=...
findings.actual: 392 out of 520 projects report a total_listings count that disagrees with the actual number of retrievable listings linked to that project_id.
findings.how_found: Counted retrievable listings grouped by project_id and compared with project.total_listings for each project.
findings.impact: Project detail cards display inaccurate listing counts if trusting the project record rather than real listing data.

findings.documented: Every listing corresponds to genuine active property data verified by the operations team.
findings.actual: At least 32 listings describe impossible physical entities: 8 negative prices (-₹7.58M to -₹19.58M), 8 impossible floor numbers (floor > total_floors), 8 with super_built_up_area < carpet_area, and 8 apartments/villas with 0 bedrooms and 0 bathrooms.
findings.how_found: Ran automated validation scripts verifying price > 0, floor <= total_floors, super_built_up_area >= carpet_area, and residential room constraints.
findings.impact: Corrupt records corrupt analytics averages, break UI floor badge logic, and show nonsensical negative pricing to end users.

findings.documented: Descriptions are seller text shown as written, and contact numbers are verified.
findings.actual: 92 listings are fraudulent advance-fee bait listings specifically designed to generate fake inquiries, demanding non-refundable booking fees ('Pay a token amount of Rs 25,000 today to block the unit', 'Site visit only after the booking amount is paid', 'Below market price, this week only').
findings.how_found: Identified text pattern clusters demanding advance token and booking amounts prior to property inspection.
findings.impact: Exposes users to real estate advance-fee scams and distorts market valuation metrics if not flagged or filtered.
